method: Original 37 roof/clerestory sample coordinates and directions are copied exactly. Reprojection uses the same 1e-5 mm inward origin offset, first-hit ray, and 0.8 mm threshold as the original screen, without moving the location. Exact original points and original chord midpoints are independently classified against r2 using nearest boundary and generic-direction parity; a longer new distance from an interior point is not called a new wall-thickness minimum. New roof warnings retain their new centroid coordinates and are supplemented by fixed source-coordinate planes, shared vertices, angle, coordinate-axis material chords, and local original-chord-midpoint cube volumes.
limitations: Boundary status is numerical (1e-6 mm); parity is a floating-point point-in-solid screen.
Every original warning remains in thin_chord_trace.json; old and new centroid minima are not directly comparable because triangulation changed.
A 1.3 mm vertical material chord describes nearby roof plate material, not an edge radius or a print guarantee.
No slicer or physical print was performed.
